chapter: Decca years and the First Herd
title: Burns today and his film music for New York, New York
summary: Burns says he no longer writes jazz; he tried to have the band used for a film but wrote music to sound like the band anyway.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: That's a rare one. Have you chatted with him in the last couple of years about doing something?
No, not -- since the anniversary was of the last time, but of course, we always talk about -- sure, we'll

have to get together and we'll do the thing." And when I've asked him to write a new piece for us, he'll say -- usually he has a -- even before the fact that I know he has more commitments than he can handle, is the fact that he'll say, I can't write any jazz, I haven't written jazz in years." One of those -- but if I could or if I was in a position -- I know for a fact that he tried very strongly to get our band to do a film he did last year, of New York, New York."
And the producer, director, whoever the person was, said he didn't want anyone so -- how do you say it, from a period that's still going or something. I don't know, it really didn't matter.

But what Ralph did anyway was to write whatever sounds there were to sound like our band. It didn't matter whether we played it or someone else did. In other words, he knew what he wanted for the period of that picture.
And for what it portrayed, as jazz musicians in life or something.
